newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares slid to the close on Wednesday after touching a four-year low as bullion sank under the $340 an ounce level.

Dealers said the metal price and the worrying prospect of very disappointing first quarter results were weighing the index, but they added that gold counters were holding their heads above water better than would be expected.
"We expected them to do a lot worse. With gold cumulatively coming down about $5 in the past 24 hours, we were expecting a bloodbath," one dealer said.
Bullion fixed $1.55 down at $339.90 on Wednesday afternoon, and was seen nearing its February 12 low of $336.15, the lowest in almost four years.
The JSE 100 percent gold index set a four year low of 1,243.6 earlier on Wednesday afternoon.
Gold shares closed 17.8 points down at 1,252.6.
June gold futures contracts eased on the day but did not finish as soft as might have been expected considering the slide in the bullion price.
The gold contract was last at 867/872 from 891 settlement.
Industrial shares finished slightly weaker after an early jump on Wall Street's overnight rally.
"The market started steady on Wall Street and moved up a but it was always very cautious," a dealer said.
"It was a moderate day but a lot of people were still nervous about Wall Street. Nobody was rushing out to buy. There really isn't much else to feed on," another dealer said.
Dealers said that much of trade took its cue from the local bond market whihc enjoyed some strength.

Further uncertainty seeped into the market as U.S. stocks shed at their start of trade, but dealers said the market was shrugging off inflationary U.S. March industrial output figures in late afternoon.
Industrial shares closed 9.2 down at 8,228.3 points and the all-share index ended 20.5 points weaker at 6,976.8.
Near-term industrial futures contracts started firm as well and saw some arbitrage coming in. But they too slowed their firming in later afternoon trade.
The June industrial contract was at 8,060/67 from 8,054, while the all-share contract was at 6,465/75 from 6,473.
Volumes traded in both futures and cash market were moderate and dealers said there was good two-way business.
Foreigner investors were absent from play but dealers said there were a number of professional punters around.
Iscor shares fell to a new year low amid gloom over possibly worse-than-expected year results, dealers said.
The share cut 12 cents off its value to 3.18 rand in heavy volume of more than four million shares.

King Food Holdings's announcement it had bought pub and restaurant chains pushed it to a new year high as well in fairly large volumes. Dealers said the news it had purchased franchised pub chains Keg and McGinty and franchised restaurant chain Saddles had been received with glee by the market.
Shares jumped to a new year high of 192 cents in early trade, up 12 cents or 6.7 percent, but by the close of trade they had lost six cents to 174 cents with 170,900 shares changing hands.
IBM South Africa Ltd toppled to another new year low after the company made a severe profit warning.
The share fell 220 cents to 10.60 rand. It was the fourth biggest percentage loser on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.

Other features included Deelkraal which was down 45 cents at 330 rand, Gencor which was off 55 cents at 18.45 rand, Rusplats which shed 175 cents to 69.50 rand and HL&H which cut 30 cents to 630 cents.
-- Melanie Cheary, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
